dispatch_boundary: Successful transport request HEADERS open. A pending policy attempt and its cause are consumed at that boundary, once even if REFUSED_STREAM triggers a transparent replacement. Unconfigured calls and the hedging executor pass no policy dispatch recorder.
qualified_cases: Unary/server-streaming: cancellation and original deadline during five-second backoff leave one execution and zero policy retries, then permit a follow-up under one-RPC admission.

Unary/server-streaming: an externally held byte-budget permit rejects the next attempt before transport open; the terminal RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED result leaves one execution and zero policy retries. Releasing that permit enables a follow-up.

Unary/server-streaming: a lifecycle queue-readiness callback cancels the retry after connection acquisition but before request HEADERS open. The open returns CANCELLED with one execution and zero policy retries; follow-up admission is reusable.

Unary/server-streaming: interrupted server pushback and attempt-timeout backoff leave policy_retries, pushback_delays and per_attempt_timeouts at zero. Eligible dispatched retry causes remain covered by the existing successful retry tests.

Unary/server-streaming: an eligible rejection, then explicit REFUSED_STREAM, then a deliberately held success response produces three peer requests but exactly one policy retry and one transparent retry. Counters are checked before the response completes, excluding both late recording and double-counted replacements.
limits: These 16 negative/positive shape and dispatch cases qualify the stated counter boundaries, not arbitrary transport schedules or a long-running fleet campaign.
